definition_en: a building where people pay to stay and eat
core_image: 夜晚亮着灯的旅馆大堂，前台后挂着房卡
scene: 我们在车站附近订了一家旅馆。We booked a hotel near the station.
sceneCN: 这里 hotel 是「旅馆」（第 1 个义项）；句意：我们在车站附近订了一家旅馆。

senses.title: A place to stay
senses.definition: a building where travellers pay for a room
senses.example: We booked a hotel near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在车站附近订了一家旅馆。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of paid lodging.
senses.whyCN: 这是付费住宿最常见的义项。

senses.title: A place with meals and service

senses.example: The hotel serves breakfast until ten.

intro.en: Hotel is a French form of the old word for a guest house.
intro.cn: hotel 是表示客舍的古老词语的法语形式。

items.en: Hospes meant host or guest.
Hospitale named a guest house.
Hostel meant a lodging place.
Hotel named a large town house.
Hotel came to mean a place for paying guests.
items.cn: hotel 转而指付费客人的住所。

note.en: Hotel is compared with look-alike words and with places to stay.
note.cn: 把 hotel 与形近词以及住宿场所作比较。

normalIntro.en: Hotel names the building where travellers pay to stay.
normalIntro.cn: hotel 指旅行者付费住宿的建筑。

normal.en: We booked a hotel near the station.
normal.cn: 我们在车站附近订了一家旅馆。

normal.en: The hotel serves breakfast until ten.
normal.cn: 这家饭店供应早餐到十点。

normal.en: Their room was on the top floor of the hotel.
normal.cn: 他们的房间在旅馆顶层。

normal.en: The hotel lobby was full of travellers.
normal.cn: 旅馆大堂里满是旅客。

normal.en: She works at a five-star hotel.
normal.cn: 她在一家五星级旅馆工作。

abstract.en: Hotel and hospital share a root: both offer shelter.
abstract.cn: hotel 与 hospital 同根：两者都提供庇护。

abstract.en: A hotel is a home that belongs to no one in particular.
abstract.cn: 旅馆是一个不属于任何特定人的家。

abstract.en: The word turns hospitality into a business.
abstract.cn: 这个词把好客之道变成了生意。

examples.en: We booked a hotel near the station.
examples.cn: 我们在车站附近订了一家旅馆。

examples.en: The hotel serves breakfast until ten.

dict_mnemonic.text: hotel 与 hostel、hospital 同源，原指接待客人的住所，后来专指付费住宿的旅馆。

root: 源自拉丁语 hospes（主人、客人）与中世纪拉丁语 hospitale（客舍），经古法语 hostel 与法语 hotel 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Hotel means a paid lodging, often with meals and service.
sensesIntro.cn: hotel 指付费住宿之处，通常也提供膳食与服务。

core.en: A shelter that welcomes paying guests.
core.cn: 接待付费客人的庇护之所。

branches.en: We booked a hotel near the station.
branches.cn: 我们在车站附近订了一家旅馆。

branches.en: Their room was on the top floor of the hotel.
branches.cn: 他们的房间在旅馆顶层。

branches.en: The hotel serves breakfast until ten.
branches.cn: 这家饭店供应早餐到十点。

branches.en: A room and a meal can both come from one hotel.
branches.cn: 一个房间和一餐饭都来自同一家旅馆。

branches.en: The hotel lobby was full of travellers.
branches.cn: 旅馆大堂里满是旅客。

intro.en: Hotel forms hotelier and shares its root with hostel and hospital.
intro.cn: hotel 可构成 hotelier，并与 hostel、hospital 同根。

latinIntro.en: The Latin hospes family spread into several English words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 hospes 一族扩散成多个英语词。

items.exampleCN: 我们享受了他们的好客。
她在一家临终关怀机构工作。

latinEntries.example: Hospitale led to hostel and hotel.
latinEntries.exampleCN: hospitale 演变为 hostel 与 hotel。

latinEntries.example: Hospes is the deepest root.
latinEntries.exampleCN: hospes 是最深层的词根。

definition_en: a period of sixty minutes, or a fixed time of day
core_image: 钟面上指针走过一大格，桌边放着一只沙漏
scene: 会议持续了三个小时。The meeting lasted three hours.
sceneCN: 这里 hour 是「小时」（第 1 个义项）；句意：会议持续了三个小时。

senses.title: A period of sixty minutes
senses.definition: a length of time equal to sixty minutes
senses.definitionCN: 等于六十分钟的一段时间
senses.example: The meeting lasted three hours.
senses.exampleCN: 会议持续了三个小时。
senses.why: This is the basic unit of time.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的时间单位。

senses.title: A fixed time of day
senses.definition: a particular time when something happens
senses.example: The shop opens during office hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店在办公时间营业。
senses.why: Here the word points to a scheduled time, not a length.
senses.whyCN: 这里指安排好的时间点而非时长。

intro.en: Hour came through Latin and French from the Greek word for a season or time.
intro.cn: hour 经拉丁语和法语来自希腊语中表示时节或时间的词。

items.en: Hora meant a season or time.
Hora meant an hour.
Hore named a fixed time.
Hour meant a twelfth part of daylight.
items.cn: hour 指白昼的十二分之一。

items.en: Hour became a fixed period of sixty minutes.
items.cn: hour 成为固定的六十分钟时段。

note.en: Hour is compared with look-alike words and with units of time.
note.cn: 把 hour 与形近词以及时间单位作比较。

normalIntro.en: Hour measures time in sixty-minute blocks and names set times of day.
normalIntro.cn: hour 用六十分钟的块来衡量时间，也指一天中固定的时刻。

normal.en: The meeting lasted three hours.
normal.cn: 会议持续了三个小时。

normal.en: We waited for hours at the airport.
normal.cn: 我们在机场等了好几个小时。

normal.en: The shop opens during office hours.
normal.cn: 这家店在办公时间营业。

normal.en: She arrived an hour before the show.
normal.cn: 她在演出开始前一小时到达。

normal.en: Avoid driving during rush hour.
normal.cn: 避免在高峰时段开车。

abstract.en: An hour is a human agreement laid over the sun.
abstract.cn: 小时是人类在太阳之上达成的一种约定。

abstract.en: The word once meant a season before it meant a clock unit.
abstract.cn: 这个词在表示钟点单位之前曾表示季节。

abstract.en: Hours feel long or short, yet the measure never changes.
abstract.cn: 小时感觉或长或短，但度量本身从不改变。

examples.en: The meeting lasted three hours.
examples.cn: 会议持续了三个小时。

examples.en: We waited for hours at the airport.
examples.cn: 我们在机场等了好几个小时。

examples.en: She arrived an hour before the show.
examples.cn: 她在演出开始前一小时到达。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 希腊 hora
dict_mnemonic.text: hour 来自希腊语 hora（时节），经拉丁语与法语进入英语，先指白昼的十二分之一，后固定为六十分钟。

root: 源自希腊语 hora（时节、时间），经拉丁语 hora 与古法语 hore 进入英语，核心是划分出来的时间段。

sensesIntro.en: Hour means a sixty-minute period or a fixed time of day.
sensesIntro.cn: hour 指六十分钟的时段，也指一天中固定的时刻。

core.en: A unit that divides the day.

branches.en: The meeting lasted three hours.
branches.cn: 会议持续了三个小时。

branches.en: We waited for hours at the airport.
branches.cn: 我们在机场等了好几个小时。

branches.en: The shop opens during office hours.
branches.cn: 这家店在办公时间营业。

branches.en: A length of time and a set time share one word.
branches.cn: 一段时间与固定时刻共用一个词。

branches.en: She arrived an hour before the show.
branches.cn: 她在演出开始前一小时到达。

intro.en: Hour forms the adjective hourly and the compound hourglass.
intro.cn: hour 可构成形容词 hourly 与复合词 hourglass。

latinIntro.en: The Latin hora came from Greek and gave English both hour and horoscope.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 hora 来自希腊语，催生了英语的 hour 与 horoscope。

items.example: The hour hand points to three.
Traffic is heavy at rush hour.

latinEntries.example: Hora gave English hour.
latinEntries.exampleCN: hora 演变为英语 hour。

latinEntries.example: Greek hora meant a season.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 希腊语 hora 意为时节。

definition_en: a building where people live, or the people living in it
core_image: 河边一栋带花园的小房子，窗户透出暖光
scene: 他们买下了一栋靠河的房子。They bought a house near the river.
sceneCN: 这里 house 是「房屋」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他们买下了一栋靠河的房子。

senses.title: A building for living
senses.definition: a building that people live in
senses.example: They bought a house near the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们买下了一栋靠河的房子。
senses.why: This is the basic sense of the building.
senses.whyCN: 这是该建筑最基本的义项。

senses.title: The people in a home
senses.definition: the people who live together in one home
senses.definitionCN: 共同居住在一个家里的人
senses.example: The whole house was asleep.
senses.exampleCN: 全家人都睡着了。
senses.why: Here the word points to the people rather than the walls.
senses.whyCN: 这里指人而非墙体。

senses.title: A chamber in government
senses.definition: one part of a law-making body
senses.example: The bill passed the lower house.
senses.exampleCN: 法案在下议院获得通过。
senses.why: This formal sense names a political chamber.
senses.whyCN: 这一正式义项指政治议事厅。

intro.en: House is an old Germanic word for a shelter.
intro.cn: house 是表示居所的古老日耳曼词。

items.en: Hus meant a dwelling.
Hus meant a house or building.
Hous kept the sense of a home.
House extended to families and chambers.
items.cn: house 扩展到家庭与议院。

items.en: Housing named the supply of homes.

note.en: House is compared with look-alike words and with words for a home.
note.cn: 把 house 与形近词以及表示住所的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: House names the building, the people inside, and even a political chamber.
normalIntro.cn: house 指建筑、屋内的人，甚至政治议事厅。

normal.en: They bought a house near the river.
normal.cn: 他们买下了一栋靠河的房子。

normal.en: The whole house was asleep.
normal.cn: 全家人都睡着了。

normal.en: We helped them move house last weekend.
normal.cn: 上周末我们帮他们搬家。

normal.en: House prices have risen this year.
normal.cn: 今年房价上涨了。

normal.en: The bill passed the lower house.
normal.cn: 法案在下议院获得通过。

abstract.en: A house is walls, but a home is the life inside them.
abstract.cn: 房子是墙，家是墙内的生活。

abstract.en: The word can hold people as easily as it holds rooms.
abstract.cn: 这个词能容纳人，就像它能容纳房间一样。

abstract.en: Politics borrowed the word for the rooms where laws are made.
abstract.cn: 政治借用了这个词来指制定法律的议事厅。

examples.en: House prices have risen this year.

dict_mnemonic.note: 义项记忆 · 房屋 → 家人 → 议院
dict_mnemonic.text: house 从「房屋」引申为「一家人」，再引申为立法机构的「议院」，都由「容纳」这一核心展开。

root: 来自古英语 hus，源于日耳曼语 hus（住所），核心义是遮风避雨的居住空间。

sensesIntro.en: House means a dwelling, the people in it, or a chamber of government.
sensesIntro.cn: house 指住宅、其中的家人，或政府的议院。

core.en: A shelter that holds people.

branches.en: They bought a house near the river.
branches.cn: 他们买下了一栋靠河的房子。

branches.en: We helped them move house last weekend.
branches.cn: 上周末我们帮他们搬家。

branches.en: The whole house was asleep.

branches.en: The walls and the family both answer to house.
branches.cn: 墙与家人都可以用 house 来指。

branches.en: The bill passed the lower house.
branches.cn: 法案在下议院获得通过。

intro.en: House yields housing, household, and housekeeper, among others.
intro.cn: house 可派生出 housing、household、housekeeper 等词。

latinIntro.en: House is Germanic; the Latin domus covers similar ground in domestic.
latinIntro.cn: house 属于日耳曼语；拉丁语 domus 在 domestic 中覆盖相似含义。

items.meaning: all the people in a home
a person who runs a home
a party for a new home

latinEntries.example: Hus is the Old English source of house.
latinEntries.exampleCN: hus 是 house 的古英语来源。

definition_en: all the people living together in one home
core_image: 一张餐桌旁坐着一家人，桌上摆着日常用品
scene: 这个家庭每月都仔细记录开支。The household records its spending carefully every month.
sceneCN: 这里 household 是「家庭」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这个家庭每月都仔细记录开支。

senses.title: All the people in a home
senses.definition: the people who live together as one unit
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个单位共同生活的人
senses.example: The household records its spending carefully every month.
senses.exampleCN: 这个家庭每月都仔细记录开支。
senses.why: This is the core sense of a domestic unit.
senses.whyCN: 这是家庭单位的核心义项。

senses.title: Relating to the home
senses.definition: connected with running a home
senses.example: Household goods are sold on the second floor.
senses.exampleCN: 家居用品在二楼出售。
senses.why: As an adjective the word describes home use.
senses.whyCN: 作形容词时描述家庭用途。

intro.en: Household joins house with hold in the old sense of possession.
intro.cn: household 把 house 与古义为「持有」的 hold 结合起来。

items.en: Hus meant a house.
Healdan meant to hold or keep.
Houshold meant the people of a house.
Household named a domestic unit.
Household became an adjective for home goods.
items.cn: household 成为描述家居用品的形容词。

note.en: Household is compared with look-alike words and with words for family groups.
note.cn: 把 household 与形近词以及表示家庭群体的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Household names a home as one unit of people and daily life.
normalIntro.cn: household 把家作为一个由人和日常生活组成的单位来称呼。

normal.en: The household records its spending carefully every month.
normal.cn: 这个家庭每月都仔细记录开支。

normal.en: All members of the household share the chores.
normal.cn: 家里所有成员分担家务。

normal.en: Household goods are sold on the second floor.
normal.cn: 家居用品在二楼出售。

normal.en: The brand became a household name.
normal.cn: 这个品牌变得家喻户晓。

normal.en: Household income rose slightly last year.
normal.cn: 去年家庭收入略有上升。

abstract.en: A household is a small economy built on shared daily needs.
abstract.cn: 家庭是建立在共同日常需求上的小型经济体。

abstract.en: To hold a house is to hold a set of relationships.
abstract.cn: 持有一个家，就是持有一组关系。

abstract.en: The word counts people the way a census counts homes.
abstract.cn: 这个词像人口普查统计住所那样统计人。

examples.en: The brand became a household name.

dict_mnemonic.note: 构词记忆 · house + hold

root: 由古英语 hus（房屋）与 healdan（持有）复合而成，原指一户人家及所掌管的家业。

sensesIntro.en: Household means the people of one home, or things used in the home.
sensesIntro.cn: household 指一屋之人，也指家庭使用的事物。

core.en: A home counted as one unit.
core.cn: 把家作为一个单位来计。

branches.en: The household records its spending carefully every month.
branches.cn: 这个家庭每月都仔细记录开支。

branches.en: All members of the household share the chores.
branches.cn: 家里所有成员分担家务。

branches.en: Household goods are sold on the second floor.
branches.cn: 家居用品在二楼出售。

branches.en: People and their goods both belong to the household.
branches.cn: 人与家用物品都属于这个家庭。

branches.en: The brand became a household name.
branches.cn: 这个品牌变得家喻户晓。

intro.en: Household forms householder and rests on house plus hold.
intro.cn: household 可构成 householder，词基是 house 与 hold。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are Germanic; the Latin equivalent appears in domestic.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都属于日耳曼语；拉丁语对应说法见于 domestic。

items.meaning: all the people in a home

latinEntries.example: Hus is the source of house.
latinEntries.exampleCN: hus 是 house 的来源。

definition_en: in what way, or to what degree

scene: 你能告诉我这台机器怎么运作吗？Can you tell me how this machine works?
sceneCN: 这里 how 是「如何」（第 1 个义项）；句意：你能告诉我这台机器怎么运作吗？

senses.title: In what way
senses.definition: in what manner or by what method
senses.example: Can you tell me how this machine works?
senses.exampleCN: 你能告诉我这台机器怎么运作吗？
senses.why: This is the core sense of asking about method.
senses.whyCN: 这是询问方法的核心义项。

senses.title: To what degree
senses.definition: to what extent or degree
senses.example: How beautiful the garden looks in spring!
senses.exampleCN: 春天的花园看起来多么美啊！
senses.why: Here the word measures degree rather than method.
senses.whyCN: 这里衡量的是程度而非方式。

intro.en: How is an old Germanic question word.
intro.cn: how 是古老的日耳曼语疑问词。

items.en: Hwo asked by what means.
Hu meant in what way.
How kept the sense of manner.
How also asks about degree and condition.
items.cn: how 也询问程度与状况。

items.en: How now opens countless everyday questions.
items.cn: how 现在引出无数日常疑问。

note.en: How is compared with look-alike words and with words about manner.
note.cn: 把 how 与形近词以及表示方式的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: How asks for a method or a degree.
normalIntro.cn: how 用来询问方式或程度。

normal.en: Can you tell me how this machine works?
normal.cn: 你能告诉我这台机器怎么运作吗？

normal.en: How do you get to the station?
normal.cn: 你怎么去车站？

normal.en: She showed me how to fold the paper.
normal.cn: 她教我怎样折纸。

normal.en: How beautiful the garden looks in spring!
normal.cn: 春天的花园看起来多么美啊！

normal.en: I do not know how he found the answer.
normal.cn: 我不知道他是怎样找到答案的。

abstract.en: How opens the door to method, the hidden shape of an action.
abstract.cn: how 打开方法之门，那是动作隐藏的形状。

abstract.en: A small question word can ask about both means and wonder.
abstract.cn: 一个小的疑问词既能问方法，也能表达惊叹。

abstract.en: Every explanation answers a how before it answers a why.
abstract.cn: 每种解释都先回答如何，再回答为何。

examples.en: Can you tell me how this machine works?

examples.en: She showed me how to fold the paper.
examples.cn: 她教我怎样折纸。

examples.en: How beautiful the garden looks in spring!

sensesIntro.en: How asks about manner or degree.
sensesIntro.cn: how 询问方式或程度。

core.en: Asking the shape of an action.

branches.en: Can you tell me how this machine works?
branches.cn: 你能告诉我这台机器怎么运作吗？

branches.en: How do you get to the station?

branches.en: One word asks both how and how much.

branches.en: She showed me how to fold the paper.
branches.cn: 她教我怎样折纸。

intro.en: How combines with ever, some, and any to form new words.
intro.cn: how 与 ever、some、any 组合构成新词。

latinIntro.en: How is Germanic; its oldest recorded form is Old English hu.
latinIntro.cn: how 属于日耳曼语，最古老的形式是古英语 hu。

items.exampleCN: 无论怎样发生，保持冷静。

latinEntries.example: Hu is the Old English source of how.

definition_en: used to introduce a contrasting point, or in whatever way
core_image: 两个人同桌，一个人点头，另一个人却摇头
scene: 雨下得很大，然而比赛仍继续进行。It was raining hard; however, the match went on.
sceneCN: 这里 however 是「然而」（第 1 个义项）；句意：雨下得很大，然而比赛仍继续进行。

senses.title: Introducing a contrast
senses.definition: used to add a statement that contrasts with what came before
senses.definitionCN: 用来引出与前述相反的说法
senses.example: It was raining hard; however, the match went on.
senses.exampleCN: 雨下得很大，然而比赛仍继续进行。
senses.why: This is the everyday contrastive use.
senses.whyCN: 这是最常见的转折用法。

senses.title: In whatever way
senses.definition: no matter how
senses.example: However hard he tried, the door would not open.
senses.exampleCN: 无论他怎么用力，门都打不开。
senses.why: Here the word means no matter how.
senses.whyCN: 这里表示「无论怎样」。

intro.en: However joins how with ever to widen a question into a concession.
intro.cn: however 把 how 与 ever 结合，把疑问扩展为让步。

items.en: Hu asked in what way.
Aefre meant ever or always.
How ever meant in whatever way.
items.cn: how ever 意为无论以何种方式。

items.en: However became a common contrast word.
items.cn: however 成为常见的转折词。

items.en: It now often stands at the start of a sentence.

note.en: However is compared with look-alike words and with contrast words.
note.cn: 把 however 与形近词以及表示转折的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: However marks a turn and can also mean no matter how.
normalIntro.cn: however 标记转折，也可表示「无论怎样」。

normal.en: It was raining hard; however, the match went on.
normal.cn: 雨下得很大，然而比赛仍继续进行。

normal.en: The plan is simple; however, it takes time.
normal.cn: 计划很简单，然而需要时间。

normal.en: However hard he tried, the door would not open.
normal.cn: 无论他怎么用力，门都打不开。

normal.en: However much it costs, we must finish.
normal.cn: 无论花多少钱，我们都必须完成。

normal.en: She was tired; however, she kept working.
normal.cn: 她很累，然而继续工作。

abstract.en: However is a hinge that lets an argument turn.
abstract.cn: however 是让论证转向的铰链。

abstract.en: The word holds two forces: contrast and unlimited degree.
abstract.cn: 这个词兼有两种力量：转折与无限程度。

abstract.en: To say however is to keep two truths standing together.
abstract.cn: 说 however 就是让两个事实并立。

examples.en: It was raining hard; however, the match went on.
examples.cn: 雨下得很大，然而比赛仍继续进行。

examples.en: However hard he tried, the door would not open.
examples.cn: 无论他怎么用力，门都打不开。

examples.en: The plan is simple; however, it takes time.
examples.cn: 计划很简单，然而需要时间。

sensesIntro.en: However marks contrast, or means no matter how.
sensesIntro.cn: however 表示转折，或表示「无论怎样」。

core.en: A turn that keeps both sides in view.
core.cn: 让两边都保留在视野中的转折。

branches.en: It was raining hard; however, the match went on.
branches.cn: 雨下得很大，然而比赛仍继续进行。

branches.en: However hard he tried, the door would not open.

branches.en: Contrast and unlimited degree share one form.

branches.en: However much it costs, we must finish.
branches.cn: 无论花多少钱，我们都必须完成。

intro.en: However belongs to the how family along with somehow and anyhow.
intro.cn: however 与 somehow、anyhow 同属 how 一族。

latinIntro.en: Both parts are Old English, so the word has no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都是古英语，因此这个词没有拉丁词根。

latinEntries.example: Hu is the base of how.
latinEntries.exampleCN: hu 是 how 的词基。

latinEntries.example: Aefre gave English ever.
latinEntries.exampleCN: aefre 演变为英语 ever。

definition_en: extremely large in size, amount, or degree
core_image: 广场中央矗立着比周围建筑还高的雕像
scene: 广场中央立着一座巨大的雕像。A huge statue stands in the middle of the square.
sceneCN: 这里 huge 是「巨大的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：广场中央立着一座巨大的雕像。

senses.title: Very large in size
senses.definition: extremely large in physical size
senses.example: A huge statue stands in the middle of the square.
senses.exampleCN: 广场中央立着一座巨大的雕像。
senses.why: This is the basic sense of physical size.
senses.whyCN: 这是体积的基本义项。

senses.title: Very great in amount
senses.definition: extremely large in amount or degree
senses.example: The company reported a huge loss.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司报告了巨额亏损。
senses.why: Here size becomes quantity or degree.
senses.whyCN: 这里体积变成了数量或程度。

intro.en: Huge came from French, probably from a Germanic word for a giant.
intro.cn: huge 来自法语，可能源于日耳曼语中表示巨人的词。

items.en: A root meaning giant or enormous stood behind the word.
items.cn: 一个意为巨人或庞大的词根藏在词后。

items.en: Ahuge meant enormous.
Huge meant very large.
Huge extended to amounts and effects.
items.cn: huge 扩展到数量与影响。

items.en: Huge is now one of the commonest size words.
items.cn: huge 现在是表示尺寸最常用的词之一。

note.en: Huge is compared with look-alike words and with words for great size.
note.cn: 把 huge 与形近词以及表示巨大的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Huge describes size that goes far beyond the ordinary.
normalIntro.cn: huge 描述远超寻常的尺寸。

normal.en: A huge statue stands in the middle of the square.
normal.cn: 广场中央立着一座巨大的雕像。

normal.en: They live in a huge house by the lake.
normal.cn: 他们住在湖边一栋巨大的房子里。

normal.en: The company reported a huge loss.
normal.cn: 这家公司报告了巨额亏损。

normal.en: A huge crowd gathered outside the hall.
normal.cn: 大厅外聚集了一大群人。

normal.en: The film was a huge success.
normal.cn: 这部电影取得了巨大成功。

abstract.en: Huge measures a gap between our body and the world.
abstract.cn: huge 衡量我们身体与世界之间的落差。

abstract.en: Size becomes feeling when the loss is huge.
abstract.cn: 当亏损是巨大的，尺寸就变成了感受。

abstract.en: The word makes the ordinary look suddenly small.
abstract.cn: 这个词让寻常之物突然显得渺小。

examples.en: A huge statue stands in the middle of the square.
examples.cn: 广场中央立着一座巨大的雕像。

examples.en: The company reported a huge loss.
examples.cn: 这家公司报告了巨额亏损。

examples.en: The film was a huge success.
examples.cn: 这部电影取得了巨大成功。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 巨人般的
dict_mnemonic.text: huge 经古法语进入英语，源头可能与「巨人」有关，所以表示体积、数量或程度上的巨大。

root: 源自古法语 ahuge（庞大的），可能进一步来自日耳曼语中表示巨人的词根。

sensesIntro.en: Huge means extremely large in size or in amount.
sensesIntro.cn: huge 表示体积极大，也表示数量或程度极大。

core.en: Size that overwhelms the ordinary.

branches.en: A huge statue stands in the middle of the square.
branches.cn: 广场中央立着一座巨大的雕像。

branches.en: They live in a huge house by the lake.
branches.cn: 他们住在湖边一栋巨大的房子里。

branches.en: The company reported a huge loss.
branches.cn: 这家公司报告了巨额亏损。

branches.en: A huge thing and a huge amount share one word.
branches.cn: 巨大的物体与巨大的数量共用一个词。

branches.en: The film was a huge success.
branches.cn: 这部电影取得了巨大成功。

intro.en: Huge forms the comparative huger and the adverb hugely.
intro.cn: huge 可构成比较级 huger 与副词 hugely。

latinIntro.en: Huge is not Latin; it arrived through French from a Germanic root.
latinIntro.cn: huge 并非拉丁语词，而是经法语来自日耳曼语词根。

items.example: It is the hugest hall here.
The hugeness of the ship amazed us.
items.exampleCN: 这艘船的巨大让我们惊叹。

items.example: A massive rock blocked the road.
A giant appeared in the story.
items.exampleCN: 故事中出现了一个巨人。

latinEntries.example: Ahuge is the French source of huge.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ahuge 是 huge 的法语来源。

definition_en: relating to people, or a person
core_image: 清晨的街道上，人们匆匆走向各自的目的地
scene: 人类已经在这片土地上生活了数千年。Humans have lived on this land for thousands of years.
sceneCN: 这里 human 是「人类」（第 1 个义项）；句意：人类已经在这片土地上生活了数千年。

senses.title: Belonging to people
senses.definition: relating to or belonging to people
senses.example: Humans have lived on this land for thousands of years.
senses.exampleCN: 人类已经在这片土地上生活了数千年。
senses.why: This is the broad sense of the species.
senses.whyCN: 这是指整个人类的广义义项。

senses.title: A person
senses.definition: a person, as opposed to an animal or machine
senses.definitionCN: 区别于动物或机器的人
senses.example: Every human needs food and rest.
senses.exampleCN: 每个人都需要食物和休息。
senses.why: As a noun the word names one person.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时指单个的人。

intro.en: Human comes from the Latin word for a person.
intro.cn: human 来自拉丁语中表示人的词。

items.en: Humanus meant of a person.
Homo meant a human being.
Humain meant human.
Human described people and their nature.
Human became a noun as well as an adjective.
items.cn: human 既是形容词也作名词。

note.en: Human is compared with look-alike words and with words for people.
note.cn: 把 human 与形近词以及表示人的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Human marks what belongs to people rather than to animals or machines.
normalIntro.cn: human 标记属于人而非动物或机器的东西。

normal.en: Humans have lived on this land for thousands of years.
normal.cn: 人类已经在这片土地上生活了数千年。

normal.en: Every human needs food and rest.
normal.cn: 每个人都需要食物和休息。

normal.en: Human rights belong to every person.
normal.cn: 人权属于每一个人。

normal.en: The human body is surprisingly strong.
normal.cn: 人体出奇地强健。

normal.en: Machines cannot replace human judgement completely.
normal.cn: 机器无法完全取代人的判断。

abstract.en: Human is a word that includes the speaker and the stranger alike.
abstract.cn: human 这个词既包括说话者，也包括陌生人。

abstract.en: To call something human is to admit both limit and dignity.
abstract.cn: 称某物为人的，就等于承认限制与尊严。

abstract.en: The word separates us from things while binding us to each other.
abstract.cn: 这个词把我们从万物中分出，又把我们彼此相连。

examples.en: Humans have lived on this land for thousands of years.
examples.cn: 人类已经在这片土地上生活了数千年。

examples.en: Every human needs food and rest.
examples.cn: 每个人都需要食物和休息。

examples.en: Machines cannot replace human judgement completely.
examples.cn: 机器无法完全取代人的判断。

dict_mnemonic.text: human 来自拉丁语 humanus，与 homo（人）同源，所以既指「人的」，也直接作名词指「人」。

root: 源自拉丁语 humanus（人的）与 homo（人），经古法语 humain 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Human describes what belongs to people, or names one person.
sensesIntro.cn: human 描述属于人的事物，也指单个的人。

core.en: Belonging to the species of people.

branches.en: Humans have lived on this land for thousands of years.
branches.cn: 人类已经在这片土地上生活了数千年。

branches.en: Machines cannot replace human judgement completely.
branches.cn: 机器无法完全取代人的判断。

branches.en: Every human needs food and rest.
branches.cn: 每个人都需要食物和休息。

branches.en: The adjective and the noun share one idea.
branches.cn: 形容词与名词共享同一个概念。

branches.en: Human rights belong to every person.
branches.cn: 人权属于每一个人。

intro.en: Human yields humanity, humane, and inhuman.
intro.cn: human 可派生 humanity、humane、inhuman 等词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root homo also appears in homicide and humus, earth.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 homo 也出现在 homicide 与表示土地的 humus 中。

latinEntries.example: Humanus gave English human.
latinEntries.exampleCN: humanus 演变为英语 human。

latinEntries.example: Homo is the Latin word for a person.
latinEntries.exampleCN: homo 是拉丁语中的人。

definition_en: needing or wanting food, or strongly wishing for something
core_image: 孩子望着餐桌上的面包，肚子咕咕作响
scene: 长跑结束后，孩子们都饿了。After the long run, the children were hungry.
sceneCN: 这里 hungry 是「饥饿的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：长跑结束后，孩子们都饿了。

senses.title: Needing food
senses.definition: feeling the need to eat
senses.example: After the long run, the children were hungry.
senses.exampleCN: 长跑结束后，孩子们都饿了。
senses.why: This is the basic bodily sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的身体感受义项。

senses.title: Strongly wishing for something
senses.definition: having a strong desire for something
senses.example: She was hungry for news of her family.
senses.exampleCN: 她渴望得到家人的消息。
senses.why: The bodily need becomes a metaphor for desire.
senses.whyCN: 身体需要变成渴望的隐喻。

intro.en: Hungry is the adjective built on the old word hunger.
intro.cn: hungry 是在古老词语 hunger 基础上构成的形容词。

items.en: Hungruz meant hunger.
Hungrig meant hungry.
Hungry meant needing food.
Hungry extended to strong desire.
Hungry for success is a common phrase today.
items.cn: hungry for success 是今天的常见说法。

note.en: Hungry is compared with look-alike words and with words for need.
note.cn: 把 hungry 与形近词以及表示需要的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Hungry names the body asking for food and the mind asking for more.
normalIntro.cn: hungry 指身体索要食物，也指心灵渴望更多。

normal.en: After the long run, the children were hungry.
normal.cn: 长跑结束后，孩子们都饿了。

normal.en: He felt hungry before dinner.
normal.cn: 晚饭前他感到饿了。

normal.en: She was hungry for news of her family.
normal.cn: 她渴望得到家人的消息。

normal.en: No child should go hungry.
normal.cn: 不该有孩子挨饿。

normal.en: The hungry dog waited by the door.
normal.cn: 饥饿的狗在门边等着。

abstract.en: Hungry is a small word for a large emptiness.
abstract.cn: hungry 是描述巨大空缺的一个小词。

abstract.en: The stomach and the heart can both be hungry.
abstract.cn: 胃与心都可以饥饿。

abstract.en: To be hungry is to be open to the world.
abstract.cn: 饥饿就是向世界敞开。

examples.en: After the long run, the children were hungry.

examples.en: She was hungry for news of her family.
examples.cn: 她渴望得到家人的消息。

examples.en: No child should go hungry.
examples.cn: 不该有孩子挨饿。

root: 来自古英语 hungrig，源于日耳曼语 hungruz，核心是身体对食物的需要。

sensesIntro.en: Hungry means needing food or strongly desiring something.
sensesIntro.cn: hungry 表示需要食物，或强烈渴望某物。

core.en: An emptiness asking to be filled.
core.cn: 一个要求被填满的空缺。

branches.en: After the long run, the children were hungry.
branches.cn: 长跑结束后，孩子们都饿了。

branches.en: The hungry dog waited by the door.
branches.cn: 饥饿的狗在门边等着。

branches.en: She was hungry for news of her family.
branches.cn: 她渴望得到家人的消息。

branches.en: Food and news can both end a hunger.
branches.cn: 食物与消息都能终结一种饥饿。

branches.en: No child should go hungry.
branches.cn: 不该有孩子挨饿。

intro.en: Hungry forms hungrier, hungriest, and the adverb hungrily.
intro.cn: hungry 可构成 hungrier、hungriest 与副词 hungrily。

latinIntro.en: Hungry is Germanic; Latin fames, hunger, survives in famine.
latinIntro.cn: hungry 属于日耳曼语；拉丁语 fames（饥饿）仍留在 famine 中。

latinEntries.example: Hungor is the Old English source of hunger.
latinEntries.exampleCN: hungor 是 hunger 的古英语来源。

definition_en: to chase animals for food or sport, or to search for something
core_image: 猎人弯腰查看雪地上的脚印
scene: 猎人在森林里寻找鹿的踪迹。The hunter hunted for deer tracks in the forest.
sceneCN: 这里 hunt 是「打猎；寻找」（第 1 个义项）；句意：猎人在森林里寻找鹿的踪迹。

senses.title: To chase animals
senses.definition: to chase and kill animals for food or sport
senses.definitionCN: 为食物或娱乐追捕并杀死动物
senses.example: The hunter hunted for deer tracks in the forest.
senses.exampleCN: 猎人在森林里寻找鹿的踪迹。
senses.why: This is the old sense of the chase.
senses.whyCN: 这是古老的追猎义项。

senses.title: To search carefully
senses.definition: to look for something with effort
senses.example: We hunted for the missing keys.
senses.exampleCN: 我们到处寻找丢失的钥匙。
senses.why: The chase becomes a search for objects.
senses.whyCN: 追猎变成对物品的搜寻。

senses.title: To pursue someone
senses.definition: to chase someone in order to catch them
senses.example: The police hunted the escaped prisoner.
senses.exampleCN: 警方追捕逃跑的囚犯。
senses.why: Here the object is a person rather than an animal.
senses.whyCN: 这里对象是人而非动物。

intro.en: Hunt is an old Germanic word for chasing game.
intro.cn: hunt 是表示追猎猎物的古老日耳曼词。

items.en: Hunton meant to chase game.
Huntian meant to hunt.
Hunt meant to chase animals.
Hunt extended to searching for things.
Job hunting made hunt a modern metaphor.
items.cn: job hunting 使 hunt 成为现代比喻。

note.en: Hunt is compared with look-alike words and with words for chasing.

normalIntro.cn: hunt 从追猎动物扩展到搜寻任何东西。

normal.en: The hunter hunted for deer tracks in the forest.
normal.cn: 猎人在森林里寻找鹿的踪迹。

normal.en: We hunted for the missing keys.
normal.cn: 我们到处寻找丢失的钥匙。

normal.en: The police hunted the escaped prisoner.
normal.cn: 警方追捕逃跑的囚犯。

normal.en: They went hunting at dawn.
normal.cn: 他们黎明时去打猎。

normal.en: She is hunting for a new job.
normal.cn: 她正在找新工作。

abstract.cn: 打猎就是沿着痕迹追踪，直到它变成具体的形体。

abstract.en: The word keeps the patience of the chase inside the search.
abstract.cn: 这个词把追猎的耐心留在搜寻之中。

abstract.en: We hunt for what we lack, not always for what we need.
abstract.cn: 我们追猎所缺，未必是所需。

definition_zh: 理想上；最好；理想情况下；以最理想的方式
definition_en: used to describe the best possible situation or outcome, or the standard one would wish to reach

sceneCN: 这里指设想最理想的状态（第 1 个义项：最佳状态）；句意为最理想的情况是，新图书馆坐落在校园的中心。场景要点：纸上的完美布局、后来才考虑的限制、校园中心的位置。

pos.zh: 理想上；最好；理想情况下

由观念名词加形容词词尾构成，义为「理想的」
由理想形容词加表示学说体系的名词尾构成，义为「理想主义」
由理想形容词加表示人的名词尾构成，义为「理想主义者」
由理想形容词加动词词尾构成，义为「把……理想化」

senses.title: The best possible state
senses.definition: describes conditions as they would be if nothing stood in the way
senses.definitionCN: 描述在没有阻碍时会呈现的那种状况
senses.example: Ideally, the new library would sit at the centre of the campus.
senses.exampleCN: 最理想的情况是，新图书馆坐落在校园的中心。
senses.why: Idea is an image in the mind, and the ideal is that image at its best.
senses.whyCN: 「观念」是心里的一幅形象，而「理想的」就是那幅形象最好的样子。

senses.title: The goal one aims at
senses.definition: names the standard that a plan or effort is trying to reach, even if it falls short
senses.definitionCN: 指出一项计划或努力试图达到的标准，即使最终达不到
senses.example: Ideally, every student would read the whole corpus before graduating.
senses.exampleCN: 理想的目标是每位学生在毕业前读完整个语料库。
senses.why: A goal is an ideal seen from the side of effort rather than from the side of fact.
senses.whyCN: 目标是从努力那一侧、而不是从事实那一侧看到的理想。

senses.title: Perfectly suited or placed
senses.definition: modifies an adjective or participle to mean perfectly suited to a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 修饰形容词或分词，表示完全适合某个用途
senses.example: The site is ideally placed for a station.
senses.exampleCN: 这块地作为车站的位置再理想不过。
senses.why: This is the manner sense: in an ideal way, not merely as a wish.
senses.whyCN: 这是方式义：以一种理想的方式，而不只是作为愿望。

senses.title: Sentence-initial planning frame
senses.definition: placed first in a plan or proposal to set out the wished-for arrangement before the constraints
senses.definitionCN: 在计划或提案中置于句首，先摆出所期望的安排，再谈限制
senses.example: Ideally, the work would be finished before the rainy season.
senses.exampleCN: 最理想的是，这项工程能在雨季之前完工。
senses.why: A plan states its ideal first so that later compromises can be measured against it.
senses.whyCN: 计划先把理想说出来，日后的让步才好拿它来量。

senses.title: The softened expectation with would
senses.titleCN: 与虚拟式连用的委婉期望
senses.definition: with would or could, softens a request or expectation so that it sounds like a wish rather than a demand
senses.definitionCN: 与虚拟式连用，把请求或期望放软，听起来像愿望而不是要求
senses.example: We would ideally like an answer by Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 最理想的是，我们希望在周五之前得到答复。
senses.why: The conditional leaves the other side room to refuse without a quarrel.
senses.whyCN: 条件式给对方留了拒绝的余地，不必吵起来。

senses.title: The opening position in a negotiation
senses.definition: in bargaining, marks the figure or terms one asks for first, knowing that the final result will be lower
senses.definitionCN: 在议价中标记最先提出的数字或条件，明知最终结果会更低
senses.example: Ideally, we would pay nothing for the first year.
senses.exampleCN: 理想的开价是，第一年我们一分钱也不付。
senses.why: An opening figure is an ideal, not a forecast, and both sides know it.
senses.whyCN: 开价是理想，不是预报，这一点双方都明白。

senses.title: The elliptical ideally, yes
senses.definition: in short replies, agrees that something is the best outcome while implying that it may not happen
senses.definitionCN: 在简短回答里承认某事是最好的结果，同时暗示它未必会发生
senses.example: Could both sides sign this week? Ideally, yes.
senses.exampleCN: 双方这周能签字吗？理想上可以。
senses.why: The short answer grants the wish without pretending that the wish is a fact.
senses.whyCN: 简短回答认可了这个愿望，却不假装愿望已成事实。

senses.title: Not the same as preferably
senses.definition: the boundary sense: ideally names the best possible state, while preferably ranks one option above another
senses.definitionCN: 分界义：这个词指出可能达到的最佳状态，而「优先」那个词只是把某个选项排在另一个之上
senses.example: Ideally the room is quiet; preferably it also has daylight.
senses.exampleCN: 最理想的是房间安静；其次最好还有自然光。
senses.why: The best state is not the same as a preference among choices.
senses.whyCN: 最佳状态与在若干选项里挑一个，并不是一回事。

senses.title: Not the same as in theory
senses.definition: the boundary sense: ideally describes a state worth reaching in practice, while in theory describes what principle says, whether or not it can be reached
senses.definitionCN: 分界义：这个词描述一个在实践中值得达到的状态，而「理论上」描述原理怎么说，无论能否达到
senses.example: In theory the system works; ideally it would also be cheap.
senses.exampleCN: 理论上这套系统行得通；最理想的是它还便宜。
senses.why: One is a goal, the other is a principle, and the difference is where each one lives.
senses.whyCN: 一个是目标，一个是原理，差别在于它们各自住在哪里。

intro.en: Ideally is ideal plus -ly. Ideal comes through French idéal from Latin idealis, from Greek idea, a form or appearance, from idein, to see. The adverb marks the way things would be at their best.
intro.cn: ideally 是 ideal 加 -ly。ideal 经法语 idéal 来自拉丁语 idealis，再上溯希腊语 idea「形相、外观」，动词为 idein「看见」。这个副词标记事物处于最好状态时的样子。

items.en: The verb meant to see, and it stands behind idea and the whole family of ideal words.
items.cn: 这个动词意为「看见」，idea 与整个「理想」词族都由它而来。

items.en: The noun named a form or appearance, and later an image in the mind.
items.cn: 这个名词指形相或外观，后来指心里的形象。

items.en: Latin borrowed the noun and used it for a mental pattern or conception.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个名词，用它指心中的模式或概念。

items.en: French formed the adjective for what exists only as a pattern to be reached.
items.cn: 法语构成这个形容词，指只作为待达到的模式而存在的东西。

items.en: English took the adjective and later the noun; the first dates are only approximate.
items.cn: 英语接收了这个形容词，后来又接收其名词用法；首次年代仅为约数。

items.en: The adverb was formed with -ly to set out the best case; the exact date of its first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 副词由 -ly 构成，用来摆出最好的情形；其首次使用的确切年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the seeing-and-image stem; the second holds the preference and principle words it is compared with.
note.cn: 第一组共享「看见与形象」的词干；第二组是拿来与它比较的偏好与原理说法。

entries.definition: A thought, plan or conception in the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 指心里的想法、计划或概念。

entries.definition: The best possible model of something, or existing only as such a model.
entries.definitionCN: 指某事最好的典范，或只作为这种典范而存在的。

entries.definition: The belief that ideals can guide reality, or a philosophical position about mind.
entries.definitionCN: 指相信理想能引导现实的立场，或关于心灵的哲学主张。

entries.definition: A person who holds to ideals, sometimes with the implication of impracticality.
entries.definitionCN: 指坚持理想的人，有时暗含不切实际之意。

entries.definition: From Old English idle, empty or unused; it means without purpose, and has nothing to do with idea.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古英语中意为「空的、未用的」的词，意为无所事事地，与「观念」毫无关系。

entries.definition: Marks which option is preferred among several, not the best possible state.
entries.definitionCN: 标记若干选项中被偏爱的一个，而不是可能的最佳状态。

entries.definition: According to principle, whether or not it can be achieved in practice.
entries.definitionCN: 指依原理而言，无论实践中能否做到。

entries.definition: Sets out a perfect situation while openly admitting that it is not this world.
entries.definitionCN: 摆出一种完美情形，同时公开承认那不是现实世界。

entries.definition: A practical request that asks for something within existing limits.
entries.definitionCN: 一种务实的请求，要求在现有条件下尽量做到。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Greek verb of seeing, the idea family, and the draftsman's first drawing.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用希腊语「看见」的动词、观念词族，以及绘图者画下的第一稿。

normal.en: Idein is to see, idea is what is seen, and ideally is how things look at their best.
normal.cn: 「看见」是看，「观念」是被看见的东西，「理想地」就是事物最好时的样子。

normal.en: Idea, ideal, idealism, idealist and ideally are one family, one root, five jobs.
normal.cn: 观念、理想的、理想主义、理想主义者与理想地：一个词族，一个词根，五份差事。

normal.en: The draftsman's first drawing is the word's home: perfect lines before the site survey.
normal.cn: 绘图者的第一稿是这个词的家乡：先有完美的线，才有场地的勘测。

normal.en: Put it before would and a demand turns into a wish.
normal.cn: 把它放在虚拟式前面，要求就变成愿望。

normal.en: Ideally, yes is an agreement with a door left open.
normal.cn: 「理想上可以」是一句留了门的同意。

abstract.en: An ideal is a map drawn before anyone has walked the ground.
abstract.cn: 理想是一张在无人走过之前就画好的地图。

abstract.en: The word describes the best case and quietly admits it is not the case.
abstract.cn: 这个词描述最好的情形，又悄悄承认它不是眼前的情形。

abstract.en: To name the best is not to promise it, and the word knows the difference.
abstract.cn: 说出最好，并不等于承诺最好；这个词懂这个区别。

examples.en: Ideally, the two departments would share a single archive.
examples.cn: 最理想的是，两个部门共用一个档案库。

examples.en: The hall is ideally suited for small concerts.
examples.cn: 这个厅非常适合举办小型音乐会。

examples.en: Ideally, we would finish the survey before the end of the month.
examples.cn: 最理想的是，我们能在月底之前完成勘测。

dict_mnemonic.note: 谐音记忆 · 非词源
dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「爱迪阿里」——先在纸上画一个最完美的版本，再谈现实：理想上、最好

root: 希腊语 idein「看见」→ idea「形相、观念」→ 拉丁语 idea → 法语 idéal → 英语 ideal，再加副词词尾构成。直接来源清楚；副词首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses differ by what the ideal is doing: describing the best state, naming a goal, modifying a fit, opening a plan, softening a request, setting an opening price, granting in a short reply, and the two boundaries against preferably and in theory.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项按「理想在做什么」分开：描述最佳状态、指出目标、修饰契合程度、开启计划、软化请求、设定开价、简短认可，以及与「优先」「理论上」的两处分界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a perfect layout drawn first on tracing paper, with the buildable part pencilled in beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：先在描图纸上画出完美的布局，再在旁边用铅笔标出现实可建的部分。

branches.en: THE BEST STATE AND THE PERFECT FIT: conditions without obstacles, and a placement that suits a purpose exactly.
branches.cn: 最佳状态与完美契合：没有阻碍的条件，以及恰好适合用途的位置。

branches.en: THE GOAL AND THE PLAN'S OPENING: a standard to reach, set out before the constraints.
branches.cn: 目标与计划的开头：一个待达到的标准，在限制之前先说出来。

branches.en: THE SOFTENED REQUEST AND THE OPENING PRICE: a wish with a conditional, a figure named first.
branches.cn: 软化的请求与开价：带条件式的愿望，以及最先报出的数字。

branches.en: THE SHORT GRANT: yes, with the door left open.
branches.cn: 简短认可：说是，同时把门留着。

branches.en: THE TWO BOUNDARIES: the best state is not a preference, and a goal is not a principle.
branches.cn: 两处分界：最佳状态不是偏好，目标也不是原理。

intro.en: Ideally is a Greek noun of seeing, filtered through Latin and French, wearing an English adjective ending and an adverb ending.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个经拉丁语与法语过滤的希腊「看见」名词，套着英语的形容词词尾与副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Greek supplies idein, idea and eidos; Latin borrowed idea and formed idealis, and French turned that into idéal before English took it.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语提供了 idein、idea 与 eidos；拉丁语借入 idea 并构成 idealis，法语把它变成 idéal，英语随后接收。

items.example: The verb is the eye behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族背后的那只眼睛。

items.example: The noun shifts from what is seen to what is conceived.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词从「被看见的」转向「被想到的」。

items.example: A related noun names the visible shape itself.
items.exampleCN: 一个相关的名词指可见的形状本身。

items.example: Latin forms the adjective for what exists as a pattern.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语构成形容词，指作为模式而存在的东西。

items.meaning: the best possible, or existing only as a model
items.meaningCN: 理想的；只作为典范存在的
items.example: English takes the adjective from French.
items.exampleCN: 英语从法语接收这个形容词。

items.example: It forms the adjective from the noun.
It forms idealism, a system of thought.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 idealism，即一套思想体系。

items.example: It forms idealist, a person who holds to ideals.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 idealist，即坚持理想的人。

items.example: It forms idealize, to treat something as perfect.

definition_en: to recognize someone or something, or to find out exactly what it is

scene: 证人从一排人中认出了嫌疑人。The witness identified the suspect in the lineup.

senses.title: To recognize
senses.definition: to recognize someone or something

senses.why: This is the everyday sense of recognition.

senses.title: To determine

definition_en: who a person is, the state of being the same, or the qualities that mark a group
core_image: 护照照片旁印着姓名与出生地
scene: 警察核对了他的身份证件。The police checked his identity papers.
sceneCN: 这里 identity 是「身份」（第 1 个义项）；句意：警察核对了他的身份证件。

senses.title: Who a person is

senses.definitionCN: 一个人是谁以及何以成为此人
senses.example: The police checked his identity papers.
senses.exampleCN: 警察核对了他的身份证件。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense used for people.
